books.name: Inversion Tower
books.focus: No sooner… · Never have I… · Little did I…

items.a: As soon as the bell rang, the students rushed out.
ans: sooner had the bell rung than
items.tip: No sooner had + subject + past participle + than… (inversion after a negative opening).
items.say: No sooner had the bell rung than the students rushed out.

items.a: I have never seen such a huge dragon.
items.tip: A negative word at the start → question order: Never have I seen…
items.say: Never have I seen such a huge dragon.

items.a: You must not open this box under any circumstances.
ans: no circumstances are you to open
items.tip: Under no circumstances + inversion: Under no circumstances must you open…
items.say: Under no circumstances must you open this box.

items.a: We only realised the map was upside down when we got lost.
items.b: It was ___ we realised the map was upside down.
ans: not until we got lost that
items.tip: It was not until … that … stresses the moment something happened.
items.say: It was not until we got lost that we realised the map was upside down.

items.a: Tickets for the concert sold out in minutes because it was so popular.
items.b: It was ___ that tickets sold out in minutes.
items.tip: such + a + adjective + noun + that…: such a popular concert that…
items.say: It was such a popular concert that tickets sold out in minutes.

items.a: If you hadn't helped me, I would have failed.
items.b: Had ___ help, I would have failed.
items.tip: Had it not been for + noun = if … hadn't been there (inverted third conditional).
items.say: Had it not been for your help, I would have failed.

items.a: Mia didn't only paint the mural; she designed it too.
items.b: Not ___ the mural, but she designed it too.
items.tip: Not only + inversion (did + subject + verb)…, but … too.
items.say: Not only did Mia paint the mural, but she designed it too.

items.a: I didn't realise how late it was.
items.tip: Little did I + verb = I didn't realise at all (formal inversion).
items.say: Little did I realise how late it was.

books.name: Wizard's Phrases
books.focus: has difficulty · put … down to · bound to · came as a surprise

items.a: Sam finds it hard to concentrate when it's noisy.
items.tip: have difficulty (in) + -ing = find it hard to…
items.say: Sam has difficulty concentrating when it's noisy.

items.a: The coach said our team's victory was due to hard training.
ans: put our team's victory down to
put the team's victory down to
items.tip: put something down to = say it was caused by.
items.say: The coach put our team's victory down to hard training.

items.a: I'm sure the rescue team will find the lost puppy.
items.b: The rescue team ___ the lost puppy.
items.tip: be bound to + verb = be certain to.
items.say: The rescue team is bound to find the lost puppy.

items.a: Everyone was surprised when the shy boy won the talent show.
ans: came as a big surprise to
came as a complete surprise to
came as a real surprise to
items.tip: come as a surprise to someone = surprise them.
items.say: The shy boy's win came as a surprise to everyone.

items.a: It's possible that the explorers took the wrong path.
items.tip: Possibility in the past: may have + past participle.
items.say: The explorers may have taken the wrong path.

items.a: Lina almost missed the train.
items.tip: narrowly avoid + -ing = almost do something (but not quite).
items.say: Lina narrowly avoided missing the train.

items.a: Nobody expected the robot to work so well.
items.tip: exceed expectations = be better than people expected.
items.say: The robot exceeded everyone's expectations.

items.a: We'd better leave now or we'll miss the fireworks.
items.b: It's ___ or we'll miss the fireworks.
items.tip: It's (high/about) time + subject + past simple = we should do it now.
items.say: It's time we left or we'll miss the fireworks.

books.name: Starry Structures
books.focus: What… was · It was … who · Having… · However hard…

items.a: Leo's kindness impressed me most.
items.tip: A cleft sentence: What + clause + was … puts the focus at the end.
items.say: What impressed me most was Leo's kindness.

items.a: Although the puzzle was hard, we solved it.
items.tip: However + adjective + subject + verb = it doesn't matter how…
items.say: However hard the puzzle was, we solved it.

items.a: Max broke the window, not Ella.
items.tip: It was + person + who… stresses who did it.
items.say: It was Max who broke the window, not Ella.

items.a: Because she had lost her key, Zara climbed in through the window.
items.b: ___, Zara climbed in through the window.
items.tip: A perfect participle clause: Having + past participle = because she had…
items.say: Having lost her key, Zara climbed in through the window.

items.a: The team trained hard, but they lost the final.
items.b: In ___, the team lost the final.
ans: spite of all their hard training
items.tip: in spite of + -ing / noun = although.
items.say: In spite of training hard, the team lost the final.

items.a: People think the old lighthouse was built by pirates.
items.b: The old lighthouse ___ built by pirates.
items.tip: People think X was… = X is thought to have been… (perfect infinitive for the past).
items.say: The old lighthouse is thought to have been built by pirates.

items.a: I'd prefer staying at home to going to the cinema.
items.tip: would sooner + verb + than + verb = would prefer.
items.say: I'd sooner stay at home than go to the cinema.

items.a: It doesn't matter what you say, I'm not eating broccoli ice cream.
items.b: No ___, I'm not eating broccoli ice cream.
items.tip: No matter what… = it doesn't matter what…
items.say: No matter what you say, I'm not eating broccoli ice cream.
